hypothesis: A base contract action (Mod 0) that is LARGE RELATIVE TO MARKET CAP predicts positive abnormal returns over 5-21 sessions, because it is new cash-flow information that is publicly announced but thinly covered. Two falsifiable shape predictions, declared now: (1) if this is underreaction to NEW information, abnormal returns must be FLAT before the action date and positive after; a pre-event run-up means the award was anticipated (solicitations are public) and the result is selection, which is exactly what killed the index-addition effect; (2) the effect must SCALE with award size over market cap, since a 50M award to Lockheed is immaterial while the same award to a 500M company is not. If it does not scale with materiality, it is not the mechanism and I will not keep it.
name: federal contract awards (USAspending, transaction-level PIT)

note: REFUTED on both pre-declared shape tests. Pre-event CAR +0.37% and post-event -0.01%; vs a same-company random-date placebo at +1.58%, event-minus-placebo is NEGATIVE (-1.21% pre, -0.06% post). Materiality rank corr +0.024, non-monotone. Implied monthly book: Sharpe 0.159, t=0.57 on 152 non-overlapping months. 27.3% of actions priceable (40.8% of dollars), 26 tickers.

hypothesis: The 41 classic technical signals were only ever tested with FIXED-HORIZON exits, which is not how anyone trades them. With a realistic exit rule they may beat simply holding the same stock for the same number of days. Rules declared NOW and deliberately NOT swept: entry at the next session's OPEN after the signal fires; stop at 2x ATR(14) below entry; target at 3x ATR(14) above; 60-session timeout; path checked against intraday low and high, and when a single bar touches both the STOP is assumed first because that is the conservative direction; costs charged at each stock's own modelled half-spread on both sides. Benchmark is buying and holding the SAME stock for the SAME realized number of days, which isolates the timing and exit rule from the market move. I am testing ONE stop/target setting taken from the literature rather than a grid, because sweeping the multiples is precisely where a technical strategy gets overfit, and a swept result would be the least trustworthy thing in this project.
name: technical signals with ATR stop/target exits, path-dependent

note: REFUTED. 13.5M simulated trades. Metric is excess over holding the SAME stock the SAME number of days, not Sharpe. Mean excess across 41 signals: -0.158%. Only 4 of 41 positive, none significant. 1 of 41 survived Benjamini-Hochberg (new_52w_high, p=0.000) and its excess is NEGATIVE at -0.05%, a reliable loser. golden_cross_50_200: net +0.54% vs +0.62% holding, excess -0.08% (t=-1.99). Signals with the biggest raw returns (gap_up +3.30%, big_down_day +2.69%) had the WORST excess, because they fire on volatile days and the stop cuts the upside. 41 names are 39 distinct tests; two were accidental duplicates.

data_window: 2023-11 to 2026-10, 730 sessions, hourly bars, ~1500 US equities
hypothesis: Twelve textbook intraday setups (opening-range break, VWAP reversion, VWAP reclaim, gap fade, gap fill, midday reversal, afternoon momentum, power hour, squeeze, volume climax, first-hour high break) beat the unconditional time-of-day return. Every entry and exit is INSIDE ONE SESSION, nothing held overnight. All parameters fixed in advance from how traders describe these setups: no threshold swept, no entry bar optimised. THE BENCHMARK IS THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS: each rule is scored against entering at the SAME bar of the session and exiting at the SAME close, but on EVERY session rather than only the ones where the signal fired. Comparing against holding from the signal bar to the close would be comparing the strategy to itself, and comparing against a full-session hold would confound the signal with a time-of-day effect. This isolates the signal's information from the fact that buying at 10:30 and selling at 16:00 has an average return of its own. New data: all 381 prior trials used daily bars, so hourly bars have never been searched here.
name: classic day-trading setups on hourly bars, same-session exit

hypothesis: Post-hoc exploration of the one intraday rule that survived trial 28. Declared AFTER the fact and counted in full, because that is what happened: a matched control (treatment vs same-volume opposite-direction vs volume-decile-matched), then 10 session-level liquidity deciles, then 10 symbol-level liquidity deciles, then 4 pooled subsets whose boundaries I chose after seeing which were positive. 24 looks plus the controls.
name: volume_climax_long: matched control plus liquidity conditioning

note: The matched control SURVIVED strongly (treatment -0.076% vs same-volume-up-close -0.209%, gross edge +0.128%, t=14.56), so the signal is real: a high-volume down bar reverts. Gross is POSITIVE at +4.94bps. But net is -7.6bps because round-trip cost is 12.5bps, and breakeven needs a 2.47bp half-spread vs 4.83bp modelled. Liquidity conditioning: FIRST ATTEMPT WAS AN ARTIFACT (split on session dollar volume, so small caps on news days landed in the top deciles; one AOSL bar at +14.42% was 4.1% of all P&L). Corrected to symbol-level liquidity: top 4 deciles net +0.054% t=2.80, survives winsorizing, BUT deciles were chosen after looking, 2023 is -0.145% and 2024 is -0.011% with only 2025 significant, and 42% of P&L sits in 10 of 580 names. The robust half of the finding is the NEGATIVE one: bottom-half liquidity nets -0.124% at t=-4.19. Not an edge.

hypothesis: The signal is a liquidity-provision signal, so it should be implemented as a maker, not a taker. Every prior simulation crossed the spread twice (2x half-spread = 12.5bps round trip) against a gross edge of 4.94bps. Posting a bid does not shrink that entry cost, it flips its sign. Declared rules, one setting, no sweep: on a high-volume down bar, post a limit bid at that bar's BID price (close x (1 - half-spread)); it fills at the first later bar in the session whose LOW touches it; exit aggressively at the session close paying one half-spread. Total cost becomes 1x half-spread instead of 2x. THE COUNTERVAILING FORCE, predicted now: a bid only fills when price continues DOWN, so fills are adversely selected and the filled subset should perform worse than the full signal. If passive entry wins, it must win AFTER that penalty. I will report the fill rate and what the unfilled signals would have done, because a maker simulation that ignores non-fills is just a taker simulation with the costs deleted. KNOWN LIMITATION: hourly bars cannot show queue position, so touching a price is treated as a fill. That is optimistic and the result is an upper bound.
name: volume_climax_long traded PASSIVELY: post a bid instead of crossing the spread

note: FAILED. Passive entry recovers the spread exactly as predicted (+0.1115% on the same bars, about 2x the 4.83bp half-spread) but adverse selection destroys far more than it saves. Fill rate 86.9%. The 13.1% of signals that do NOT fill return +0.4904% as a taker (t=17.19); the 86.9% that DO fill return -0.1612% (t=-6.67). Gap -0.6515%. A bid only fills when price keeps falling, so posting it forfeits precisely the trades that worked. Passive on filled bars nets -0.0497% with t=0.38, p=0.700: negative and now indistinguishable from zero. And this is an UPPER BOUND, since hourly bars treat touching a price as a fill when queue position means it often is not. NOTE the trap: the +0.49% on unfilled bars is not tradeable, because 'will never trade below this price again' is only knowable after the fact.

data_window: 2023-11 to 2026-10 hourly, VIX from the prior close
hypothesis: Nagel (Evaporating Liquidity, RFS 2012) finds short-term reversal returns are compensation for liquidity provision and that the expected return is strongly time-varying and predictable with VIX, because liquidity supply withdraws during stress. If our +4.94bp gross effect is that premium, it must GROW with market stress. Declared now: sessions split into VIX TERCILES (not deciles, to keep the search small) using the PRIOR session's VIX close, never the same day's, because same-day VIX is contemporaneous with the price action being measured. FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION: the treatment-minus-control edge rises monotonically from the low to the high VIX tercile. If it does not, Nagel's mechanism does not apply here and the liquidity-provision story for our result is WRONG, which would also undercut the interpretation I have been giving it. Secondary question: does net return after the 12.5bp round-trip cost turn positive in the high-VIX tercile.
name: volume_climax_long conditioned on VIX: does the liquidity premium scale with stress?

note: PREDICTION CONFIRMED. Nagel's stress-dependence holds: edge rises monotonically +0.0852% (VIX 11.9-15.3) -> +0.1432% (15.3-17.8) -> +0.1594% (17.8-52.3), each tercile independently significant at t=8.04, 8.91, 8.28. The rise comes from the TREATMENT improving (+0.0166% -> +0.1063%) rather than the control worsening, which is the right mechanism: the reversal premium itself grows when liquidity withdraws. Net after costs moves from -0.1154% at low VIX to -0.0067% at high VIX, i.e. essentially BREAKEVEN but still not positive. Gross 10.63bp vs cost ~11.3bp in the high tercile: short by 0.67bp. The liquidity-provision interpretation is now supported by its own stress dependence rather than only asserted.

hypothesis: The whole project's cost numbers came from a volume heuristic I wrote. The high-VIX intraday result landed 0.67bp from breakeven, inside that heuristic's error, so the cost model was carrying the conclusion. EDGE (Ardia, Guidotti, Kroencke, JFE 2024) estimates the effective spread from OHLC. Validated on synthetic bars first (errors -0.10 to +1.03bp over 2-50bp). Question: does the high-VIX net turn positive, negative, or stay ambiguous when costs are measured rather than assumed?
name: measure spreads with EDGE instead of modelling them

note: RESOLVED AGAINST THE STRATEGY. Measured round-trip cost in the high-VIX tercile is 16.50bp against 10.77bp gross, so net is -5.73bp, not the -0.50bp my model implied. The gap is 8.5x wider than I thought. THE REASON IS INSTRUCTIVE: a volume-based cost model gets stress BACKWARDS. My model had costs FALLING in high VIX (14.79 -> 11.27bp) because volume rises under stress; measured spreads RISE (15.40 -> 16.50bp). Volume and spread both increase in a sell-off and the heuristic only saw the volume. That single error is what made the result look like breakeven. Also fixed a bug of my own: the first EDGE run strung each symbol's month of hourly bars together, so every 7th transition was an overnight gap of 0.4-0.8% read as bid-ask bounce, returning a 9.82bp half-spread for stocks trading 627M a day with no liquidity gradient at all. Per-session estimation fixed it (AAPL 7.09 -> 1.73bp) and raised correlation with the old model from 0.076 to 0.481. CAVEAT: EDGE still likely overstates spreads for mega-caps (3.35bp at the top decile vs a true ~0.3-0.5bp), so true cost sits between the two estimates; at their midpoint net is still -3.1bp, and the stress direction that kills it is robust either way.

hypothesis: SetupAlpha's calendar section claims 'a mean-reversion strategy that also incorporates turn-of-month timing can significantly outperform the same strategy traded any day of the month'. Testing both halves. TOM window declared as the last 1 trading day of a month plus the first 3 of the next, the standard Lakonishok-Smidt definition, NOT tuned. Mean reversion declared as buying the bottom-decile 5-day return, cross-sectionally, held 5 sessions. FALSIFIABLE: (1) TOM-window returns exceed non-TOM returns net of measured costs; (2) the stacked version beats mean reversion alone by more than the TOM effect alone would imply, which is what 'significantly outperform' has to mean. Costs from EDGE-measured spreads, not modelled. The article gives no figures for this claim, so there is no number to replicate, only a direction.
name: turn-of-month effect, alone and stacked with mean reversion

note: SetupAlpha's stacking claim REFUTED. Mean reversion in the TOM window returns +0.5782% vs +0.6555% outside it, so stacking gain is NEGATIVE at -0.0626%. The strategy does WORSE at the turn of the month, not better. TOM on its own is +0.4794% vs +0.3348% for the rest of the month, but on only 122 independent observations at t=0.89, which is not significant. The mean-reversion book itself prints +0.5262% net per 5 sessions, +27.26% annualised, and I do NOT believe it: the universe is today's index members, so buying the bottom decile of 5-day losers (median loss -7.38%) systematically excludes every loser that kept falling and left the index. That is the most survivorship-sensitive strategy constructible on a survivorship-biased universe. Costs are NOT the explanation (losers sit at 44M median ADV vs 47M universe median, so ~13bp not far off the 11.46bp used).

REFUTED, after a lookahead fix. 4.3M intraday trades across 12 declared day-trading rules, 1,489 symbols, 720 sessions, same-session exit. ALL 12 have negative net return after EDGE-measured costs; the only positive net is gap_down_fill at +0.036% with p=0.988. Mean excess over the unconditional time-of-day return: +0.0016%. IMPORTANT: the first version of this run was contaminated. Two rules (volume_climax_long, vwap_reversion_long) compared a bar to SESSION-WIDE statistics that included bars after the entry. volume_climax_long's apparent edge fell from +0.065% to +0.002% once the volume baseline was made causal, so 97% of it was the bug. tests/test_no_lookahead_intraday.py now swaps the future between sessions and requires decisions at bars 0..i to be unchanged; it reports INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS when a rule fires too rarely to prove anything, which is how the first version of the test wrongly passed the contaminated rule.

hypothesis: MECHANISM limited investor attention (Hirshleifer-Teoh, Hou-Peng-Xiong). PEAD already died here because surprise magnitude correlated +0.104 with 126-day momentum, i.e. it was momentum in a costume. This is a DIFFERENT hypothesis: not 'big surprise predicts drift' but 'LOW ATTENTION predicts slow diffusion'. Attention is proxied by announcement-day volume relative to the stock's own trailing 60-day volume, which is a within-stock measure and so is not a size or liquidity proxy. PREDICTION post-announcement drift is LARGER for low-attention announcements, conditional on the same surprise. The interaction is the test, not the main effect. NULL no difference in drift between attention terciles. FALSIFICATION if drift does not increase monotonically as attention falls, or if the effect vanishes after residualising against beta, size and 126-day momentum, the mechanism is rejected and I will not retest it with a different attention proxy. HORIZON 21 sessions, chosen because Bernard-Thomas find drift persisting ~60 sessions and 21 is the shortest horizon the cost screen permits (0.9-2.1% annual drag at monthly turnover vs 18.7-43.9% daily). INFORMATION AVAILABILITY uses tradeable_from, never announcement timestamp. COST FEASIBILITY needs >9.46bp gross per round trip under scenario B. UNIVERSE A (current constituents), which is MEASURED to be missing 37% of names; this is a Level 1-2 predictive test and no feasibility claim will be made from it.
name: H1 limited attention: earnings diffuse slower in low-attention names

hypothesis: MECHANISM information decays between mandatory filings. The longer since a company last filed, the wider the market's uncertainty about its true state, and uncertainty that cannot be diversified should be compensated. NOBODY HAS TESTED THIS HERE; previous fundamental work used the VALUES in filings (earnings yield, accruals, ROE), never the AGE of the information. PREDICTION stocks with the staleest fundamentals, measured as sessions since the last SEC filing date, earn higher subsequent returns than freshly-filed stocks in the same sector. NULL no monotone relationship between information age and forward return. FALSIFICATION if the relationship is non-monotone, or reverses, or disappears once sector and size are controlled, the uncertainty-premium reading is rejected. A KNOWN CONFOUND, stated now: filing age is mechanically tied to the fiscal calendar, so any effect could be a seasonality artifact rather than an uncertainty premium; the test therefore controls for calendar month and the control is part of the prediction, not an afterthought. HORIZON 21 sessions. INFORMATION AVAILABILITY the fundamentals table is keyed on SEC filed date, which is exactly the point-in-time field this needs. UNIVERSE A, 37% missing, Level 1-2 only.
name: H2 information age: stale fundamentals carry an uncertainty premium

hypothesis: MECHANISM compensation for providing liquidity to forced sellers (Nagel 2012, Evaporating Liquidity). This project already found that effect intraday and it died twice: once because the signal read future volume, and once because 10.77bp of gross cannot pay a 16.50bp round trip. The mechanism was never the problem; the HORIZON was. At 21-session holding the measured cost drag is 0.9-2.1% a year instead of 18.7-43.9%, a 20x difference, so this tests the SAME mechanism at the only horizon where the arithmetic permits it. PREDICTION stocks with the largest 5-day declines ACCOMPANIED BY abnormal volume outperform over the following 21 sessions, relative to equally-declined stocks WITHOUT abnormal volume. The volume condition is the mechanism: forced selling leaves a volume signature, ordinary drift does not. The matched control is the test. NULL no difference between high-volume and low-volume decliners. FALSIFICATION if the two groups do not separate, the forced-selling reading is rejected. VOLUME BASELINE strictly causal, trailing 20 sessions excluding the current one, because the intraday version of this hypothesis was destroyed by exactly that error. SURVIVORSHIP WARNING this hypothesis buys recent losers and the universe is MEASURED to be missing 37% of names, disproportionately the acquired ones; a positive result here is the one most likely to be survivorship and will be reported with that attached.
name: H3 liquidity provision at a horizon the cost structure actually permits

note: H1 REFUTED WITH THE SIGN REVERSED. Predicted: low attention -> MORE drift. Found: low-minus-high attention drift is NEGATIVE in all three surprise terciles (-0.426%, -0.109%, -0.153%), so HIGH-attention announcements drift more, not less. Residualised IC -0.0029 at t=0.36 on 23 independent observations, non-monotone. The limited-attention reading is rejected. Per the registration I will not retest this with a different attention proxy.

H2 REFUTED. Information age carries no predictive content. IC raw -0.0006 (t=0.67), residualised -0.0029 (t=0.21), non-monotone across quintiles, on 1.49M observations and 146 independent periods. Sample size is not the limitation here; the effect is absent. The uncertainty-premium reading is rejected.

H3 REFUTED WITH THE SIGN REVERSED, and the reversal is informative. Predicted: 5-day losers WITH a forced-selling volume signature outperform those without. Found the opposite: with signature +0.711%, without +1.493%, separation -0.782% over 21 sessions on 435K observations. High-volume declines predict WORSE subsequent returns. Reading: at a 21-day horizon the volume signature marks INFORMATION, not liquidity. A decline on heavy volume is news being priced; a decline on light volume is noise that mean-reverts. Nagel's liquidity premium is an intraday-to-few-day phenomenon and by 21 sessions the information content dominates. This is consistent with the intraday work: the mechanism is real at short horizons where it cannot pay for itself, and absent at long horizons where it could. NOTE the signal here is binary so rank IC is the wrong statistic; the direct group comparison is the test and it is decisively negative.

hypothesis: MECHANISM this is how real funds get from 2bp of IC to a tradeable book. They do not trade one signal; they combine many weak, loosely-correlated signals. The Fundamental Law says K uncorrelated signals of equal IC combine to roughly IC x sqrt(K). This project has only ever tested signals INDIVIDUALLY or in naive equal-weight sleeves, which is the one methodological gap where our approach genuinely differs from a professional one in a way that favours them. PREDICTION, falsifiable: the combined signal's IC exceeds the BEST individual signal's IC by a factor near sqrt(K_effective), where K_effective is the participation ratio of the signal correlation matrix eigenvalues, NOT the raw count. If combining adds nothing beyond the best single signal, diversification across signals is not the missing piece and I will stop claiming it might be. NULL combined IC <= best individual IC. WEIGHTS equal-weight, plus an expanding-window inverse-volatility variant that uses only each signal's past volatility and NEVER its past mean, so a signal cannot earn weight by having been profitable in sample. No optimised weights, because fitting weights on the full sample is the purest form of the overfitting this project exists to prevent. HORIZON 21 sessions. UNIVERSE A, measured to be missing 37% of names. Costs scored against the four measured scenarios.
name: combined portfolio from weak signals: does diversification across signals rescue them?

note: REFUTED, and informatively. The diversification WAS genuinely available: 11 signals, mean absolute pairwise correlation only 0.099, K_effective 7.85 of 11, so the law offered sqrt(7.85)=2.80x. Combining DELIVERED 0.71x, i.e. the combined signal is WORSE than the best single one (equal weight IC 0.0083 vs rev5 at 0.0116; inverse-vol worse still at 0.0048). WHY: sqrt(K) assumes K signals of similar POSITIVE IC. The actual distribution is wildly uneven. rev5 0.0116 and rev21 0.0106 carry almost everything; lowvol is -0.0050 and near52w is -0.0013, both NEGATIVE; si_ratio 0.0004, si_chg 0.0002, volshock 0.0010 and mom126 0.0012 are indistinguishable from zero. Equal-weighting dilutes the two that work with nine that do not. This replicates at the SIGNAL level what the breadth work found at the sleeve level: more independent bets do not help when the new bets are bad bets. So signal combination is NOT the missing piece, and the gap between this project and a professional operation is not that we failed to combine. NOTE a legitimate follow-up exists and was deliberately NOT run: selecting signals on an expanding window of their own PAST IC would be causal and would likely improve this. Selecting them on their full-sample IC, which is what the eye wants to do here, is selection on the answer.

hypothesis: CLAIM under test (CodeTrading, 'How to Spot and Avoid Overfitting', qFSuXygdOKo): leave indicators at defaults, tune only take-profit and stop-loss, and an indicator whose TP/SL heatmap is positive across most cells is robust. TEST: 12 existing intraday rules (entries from the post-lookahead-fix trades file) x 5 stop multiples {0.5,1,1.5,2,3} x 5 target multiples {0.5,1,1.5,2,3}, in units of the symbol's trailing 20-session mean hourly range (excluding the current session). Exit at first touch, stop assumed first if both in one bar, otherwise at the session close. Cost = 2 x measured EDGE half-spread for the symbol-month. Every cell scored TWO ways: (a) the video's way, raw net return; (b) excess over entering at the same bar with the same exits on EVERY session of that symbol. PREDICTION: (a) will look greener than (b); (b) will be mostly red because measured gross edges (best 4.5bp) are a third of the 13bp round trip and exits cannot manufacture edge. PASS = a rule with positive excess in >=80% of its cells AND at least one cell surviving BH across all 300. Counted as 300 trials because a sweep is a sweep.
name: TP/SL heatmap on the 12 intraday rules (CodeTrading overfitting video)

note: SIGNAL YES, TRADE NO. Raw net (the video's metric) green in 0 of 300 cells: every rule loses money after the measured 13-15bp EDGE round trip at every stop/target. Gross green 38%. Excess over same-bar same-exit every-session benchmark green 43%; 103/300 cells pass BH. Two rules meet the declared excess pass bar: vwap_reversion_long (25/25 cells positive, best +10.3bp excess, t=6.3, gross +9.6bp vs ~13.4bp cost -> net -3.7bp) and volume_climax_long (best +4.9bp excess, gross +4.2bp vs 15.3bp cost -> net -11.2bp). The pass bar was mis-specified: excess measures information, not tradeability, and I record that rather than claim a pass. RECONCILIATION: original intraday_study excess for vwap_reversion_long was +0.9bp because its printed mean was trade-weighted; session-weighted (what its own t-stat used) is +11bp. Effect concentrates on quiet days with few firings and vanishes on broad selloff days when hundreds fire. Exits shape the map (wider targets better, tight stops worse) but no cell turns any rule net positive. A mega-cap-only cut (7.4bp round trip < 9.6bp gross) is an obvious follow-up and would be a NEW declared trial chosen after seeing this data, not run here.

hypothesis: User's challenge: fixed-distance stops/targets and selling at the close are not how traders exit. TEST: same 12 rules, same entries (post-fix trades file, entry at close of signal bar), four exit styles, all causal, all with a protective stop of 1x the trailing 20-session mean hourly range: (1) RESISTANCE target = nearest level above entry among {session high through the signal bar, prior session high}; (2) VWAP target = session VWAP through the signal bar, if above entry; (3) BREAKEVEN: once a bar's high reaches entry+1R, the stop moves to entry from the NEXT bar; (4) TRAILING: stop = highest high since entry minus 1R, updated after each bar closes. If no exit, out at the session close (day trading, never overnight). Within a bar the stop is checked first. Gaps through a level fill at the bar open. Cost = 2 x previous-month EDGE half-spread. PASS BAR (corrected after trial 38 mis-specified it): the trade must make money, i.e. mean NET return > 0 both trade-weighted and session-weighted, AND the session-level t-test of net > 0 survives BH across all 48. Excess over the every-session benchmark is reported but is NOT the pass bar. PREDICTION: still 0 pass; VWAP target is the most plausible, since vwap_reversion_long earns +9.6bp gross and needs ~4bp more.
name: realistic exits on the 12 intraday rules: resistance, VWAP, breakeven, trailing

note: REFUTED, 0 of 48 pass; 0 of 48 have positive net per trade. Realistic exits (resistance target, VWAP target, breakeven stop, trailing stop, all with 1R protective stop) made the best rule WORSE than simply holding to the close. vwap_reversion_long net per day: hold-to-close (trial 38 widest cell) -3.7bp; breakeven -4.0; trailing -4.8; resistance -4.9; VWAP target -6.7. Gross per day 9.4 / 8.6 / 8.5 / 6.7 vs ~9.6 for hold. Taking profit at VWAP, the 'obvious' exit for a VWAP reversion, is the worst: it caps winners at the mean while the stop leaves losers their full 1R, and the reversion apparently overshoots VWAP into the close. Trade-weighted net is -12 to -22bp everywhere because the effect lives on quiet days (see trial 38 reconciliation). Best exit per rule ranges -8.5bp (gap_down_fill breakeven) to -18.8bp. Lesson: exits redistribute an entry's move; they did not add to it here, and every active exit cost gross relative to holding.

hypothesis: MECHANISM: every single rule's gross move (~0-10bp) is below the ~13bp round trip. If rules carry partly independent information, requiring k of them to fire on the same stock the same session should raise gross per trade (fewer, better trades), which is the only lever that can beat a fixed per-trade cost. Running rules side by side cannot help: summing negative-net books stays negative. TEST: entry at the close of the bar where the k-th rule fires that session (all 12 rules are long entries; first firing per rule from the post-fix trades file), hold to the session close (the best exit in trials 38-39), cost = 2 x previous-month EDGE half-spread. VARIANTS (5): (A) count over ALL 12 rules, k = 2, 3, 4 -- no selection, clean; (B) count over the buy-weakness family {vwap_reversion_long, volume_climax_long, midday_reversal, opening_range_break_down, gap_down_fill}, k = 2, 3 -- grouped by mechanism, BUT I have seen trials 38/39 and these overlap the rules that showed positive excess, so B is contaminated by selection and any pass in B alone counts for little. k=1 is reported as the reference and not counted (already tested). PASS BAR: net per trade > 0 both trade-weighted and session-weighted, AND session-level one-sided t-test of net > 0 survives BH across the 5. PREDICTION: gross rises with k but net stays negative in A; B is the only plausible pass.
name: confluence: trade only when several intraday rules agree on the same stock-session

note: REFUTED, 0 of 5 pass; prediction 'gross rises with k' also wrong. (A) all 12 rules: gross per trade FALLS as more rules agree: k=1 -0.0bp, k=2 -0.7, k=3 -1.0, k=4 -1.2; net -13.1 -> -14.6bp. Design weakness found: k=2 fires on 1.01M of 1.015M stock-sessions, because several rules (inside_session_squeeze, power_hour_long, afternoon_momentum, midday_reversal) fire on roughly half of all sessions, so 'agreement' among near-always-on rules is not confirmation. (B) buy-weakness family, chosen post hoc: gross per trade 1.9 -> 0.8 -> 0.5bp at k=1/2/3; per-day 5.8 -> 7.5 -> 6.8bp, net per day -7.6 / -6.1 / -7.1bp, t of net all negative. Reading: the rules are redundant, not independent; a second rule firing restates the first (same dip measured two ways) and adds no information, so confluence cuts trade count without raising the move per trade. Same lesson as trial 37 at the daily level.

hypothesis: MECHANISM: across trials 38-40 the binding constraint is cost: gross ~0-10bp per trade vs a ~13bp round trip. Go where the round trip is smaller. (1) MEGA-CAPS: each month, the 50 symbols with the highest median daily dollar volume in the PREVIOUS month (causal membership). Same 12 rules, same entries from the post-fix trades file. CAVEAT: this test was chosen after seeing vwap_reversion_long's +9.6bp gross vs the 7.4bp mega-cap spread, so it is contaminated by selection; recorded here so a pass is read with that in mind. hypothesis: MECHANISM (Gao, Han, Li & Zhou 2018, JFE 'Market intraday momentum'; Baltussen, Da, Lammers & Martens 2021 on gamma hedging): leveraged-ETF rebalancing and option dealers' hedging push the market in the direction of the day's move into the close, and late-informed traders act near the close. Counterparties: mechanical rebalancers who must trade at the close regardless of price. SPEC, one primary, fixed now: for each of SPY, QQQ, IWM, predictor r1 = close of the 09:30-10:30 bar / previous session close - 1 (overnight plus first hour, as in the paper with hourly bars replacing half-hours). At 15:30 (close of the 14:30 bar), go LONG if r1 > 0, SHORT if r1 < 0, exit at the 16:00 close. Fixed notional per ETF per day (equal thirds of capital), so sizing is causal. Every session with a prior close counts; nothing is skipped. SCORING via evaluation.py: per-trade mean with session-clustered SE; daily P&L series; Sharpe annualized at 252. COST: a conservative 2bp round trip (one-cent floors are 0.17/0.19/0.45bp for SPY/QQQ/IWM; 2bp allows ~5-10x for slippage). PASS, both required: (1) net-of-2bp per-trade mean has clustered t >= 2.0; (2) net daily Sharpe exceeds the luck bar at N = declared studies (43) for 700 daily observations, 1.331. Also reported, not the bar: gross, break-even cost, per-ETF, by-year, beta to SPY, bar at raw N (1.923). PREDICTION: effect is published and well known since 2018, so expect it to be weaker than the paper; plausible gross 1-3bp, likely FAILS. The data was pulled for trial 41 but this signal was never computed on it.

hypothesis: MECHANISM (Lou, Polk & Skouras 2019; Bogousslavsky 2021; Lachance 2023): US equity returns accrue overnight because holding overnight is costlier for arbitrageurs (higher margin, lending fees charged on overnight positions), so they flatten into the close and are paid to bear overnight risk. Trial 17 found it real (overnight Sharpe 0.83 across 4.4m stock-days, 62% of return) but untradeable under a volume-based cost model (~2bp half-spread for large caps, crossing twice daily). The 2026-10-14 audit found the project's cost models overstate costs for expensive liquid names. The realistic execution is the AUCTIONS: market-on-close buy, market-on-open sell, filled at the official close and open prints, so no spread is crossed. SPEC: universe each month = 50 stocks with highest median daily dollar volume in the PREVIOUS month (causal). Every trading day, buy each at the close, sell at the next open, equal weight. Prices dividend- and split-adjusted by applying each day's adj_close/close factor to that day's open. COST: 1bp round trip (exchange auction fees ~0.03-0.1bp, SEC fee ~0.3bp on sells, the rest for auction impact at small size). PASS, all three required: (1) net mean daily return clustered t >= 2.0; (2) net daily Sharpe > luck bar at N = declared studies (44) for ~3,190 daily obs: 0.626; (3) net Sharpe > the Sharpe of simply HOLDING the same names (equal weight, close to close, same monthly membership), because a strategy that is long the market part-time is only worth running if it is better risk-adjusted than holding. Descriptive only: SPY overnight, by year, cost sensitivity 0.5/2/4bp, beta to SPY, and the long-overnight/short-intraday spread. CAVEAT: the daily database is today's universe, so it is survivor-biased; both the strategy and the hold benchmark share it. Raw-N bar 0.901 also reported.

hypothesis: MECHANISM (Harris & Gurel 1986; Petajisto 2011; Chen, Noronha & Singal 2004): index funds must sell a deleted stock, and they do it in the closing auction of the last session BEFORE the effective date, regardless of price. RE-SPECIFICATION, declared as such: trial 19 bought deletions at the close OF the effective date, one session AFTER the forced selling, and found +0.59% t=0.67. If the bounce is fast it was missed. This test moves the entry to the rebalance close itself. That change is motivated by the mechanism but chosen after trial 19 failed, so it is contaminated; recorded so. SAMPLE: every S&P 500 deletion with effective date 2014-01-01 onward in the Wikipedia change table (oldid 1368152951, 2026-08-07) whose stated reason is a market-capitalization change or no longer representative (107 events). Acquisitions, mergers, spin-offs, renames, bank failures and unexplained 'X replaces Y' rows excluded. Prices from the database, else yfinance; events without a price at entry are dropped and counted. TRADE: buy at the close of the last trading session before the effective date (market-on-close), sell at the close 5 sessions later (market-on-close). Return is market-adjusted: minus SPY over the same window. COST: 20bp round trip (auctions on both legs, but demoted names are smaller and the entry auction is one-sided). SCORING: evaluation.clustered_mean, clustered by entry date. PASS: mean market-adjusted net return > 0 with clustered t >= 2.0. POWER: ~100 events at ~6% five-day vol gives a minimum detectable effect near 1.7%; a smaller true bounce would not be seen, and that will be reported. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: trial 19's timing (entry at the effective-date close) on the same events, to isolate the first session; 1- and 10-session horizons; additions shorted at the same rebalance close.

hypothesis: MECHANISM (Faber 2007; Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen 2012; Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen 2017): trends persist because investors under-react, then over-react, and because risk-off selling cascades. A trend filter cannot beat the market on return in a rising market; its claim is RISK-ADJUSTED: it sidesteps the large drawdowns (2000-02, 2008) at the cost of lag. RULE, fixed from Faber 2007 with no tuning: at each month-end, if SPY's total-return close is above its 10-month simple moving average of month-end closes, hold SPY for the next month; otherwise hold T-bills (13-week rate, ^IRX). One switch costs 2bp. DATA: SPY daily total return (yfinance, auto-adjusted) and ^IRX, 1993-01-29 to 2026-10-06; nothing on or after the 2026-10-07 lockbox seal. EVALUATION: monthly returns in excess of T-bills, Sharpe annualized at 12. 1993-2013 is reported as the published-era period (the rule came from it, so it is not evidence). PASS, all on the 2014-01 to 2026-09 HOLDOUT, all required: (1) strategy Sharpe > buy-and-hold SPY Sharpe; (2) strategy max drawdown smaller than buy-and-hold's; (3) a Memmel-corrected Jobson-Korkie test of the Sharpe difference is reported (not required, since 12 years cannot resolve small differences). Descriptive only: the 200-day daily variant, and the 1993-2013 period. PREDICTION: lower drawdown, similar or lower Sharpe since 2014, because the 2018, 2020 and 2022 dips reversed fast and whipsaw costs the filter.

hypothesis: MECHANISM (Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999, industry momentum; Faber 2010 relative strength): sector trends persist because news diffuses slowly across industries and institutional flows chase recent winners for months. Sector-level momentum is better documented than single-stock technical patterns and trades monthly, so costs are trivial. Never tested in this project. RULE, fixed now: universe = the 9 original SPDR sector ETFs (XLB XLE XLF XLI XLK XLP XLU XLV XLY; XLRE and XLC excluded because they start in 2015 and 2018). At each month-end rank by total return from 12 months ago to 1 month ago (skipping the latest month, as in the literature), hold the top 3 equally next month. Cost 2bp per unit of one-way turnover. Data: yfinance auto-adjusted daily closes, 1998-12-22 to 2026-10-06. BENCHMARK: the 9 sectors equal-weighted, rebalanced monthly (the fair comparison: same assets, no signal); SPY reported too. PASS, both: (1) monthly return over the equal-weight benchmark has t >= 2.0 over the full 1999-2026 period (all of it after the 1999 publication); (2) strategy Sharpe > equal-weight benchmark Sharpe. Descriptive only: 2014-2026, SPY comparison, top-1 and top-5 variants, max drawdown.
name: sector rotation by relative strength: top 3 of 9 SPDR sectors on 12-1 month momentum

hypothesis: MECHANISM (Jegadeesh 1990; Lehmann 1990; Nagel 2012): short-term losers rebound because market makers and liquidity providers absorb selling pressure and are paid for it; the reversal is compensation for supplying liquidity, larger when liquidity is scarce. In this project rev5 was the strongest daily signal (IC 0.0116, t=1.82, trial 37) and trial 46 found RSI<30 stocks rebound +5.5% when no stop cuts them out. Never tested as a weekly book. RULE: every 5 sessions, universe = 500 stocks with the highest median daily dollar volume in the previous calendar month (causal). Signal = total return over the 5 sessions ending at day t's close. Buy the bottom decile (50 biggest losers) equally at day t+1's OPEN (never the signal close, which avoids bid-ask bounce), sell at day t+6's open. Non-overlapping weeks. COST: 5bp round trip on the loser book (large caps; the audit showed no spread was measured, so the break-even cost is also reported and is the more robust number). BENCHMARK: the same 500-stock universe equal-weighted over the same open-to-open week, no trading cost (it is the passive alternative). SCORING: weekly series. PASS, both: (1) weekly excess return (losers net minus universe) has t >= 2.0; (2) annualized Sharpe of the loser book net > the universe's Sharpe. Descriptive only: break-even cost, the top decile (winners), long-losers/short-winners spread, by-year, VIX-high weeks (Nagel's prediction).
name: short-term reversal: buy last week's biggest losers among the 500 most liquid stocks

note: FAIL on excess t (both required). 2000-01 to 2026-10, 322 months, all after the 1999 publication: top 3 of 9 SPDR sectors by 12-1 month return, +9.5%/yr, vol 15.0%, Sharpe 0.68, max DD -41.2% vs all 9 equal-weight +8.8%, 14.7%, 0.65, -49.1% (SPY 0.61). Losers are just higher-beta: same mean, more volatility. Long losers/short winners -9.1bp/week, t=-0.78 (winners kept winning slightly, +5.3bp). Hit rate 50%. data_window: train/validate 2014-2019, test 2020-01 to 2026-09 (data before the 2026-10-07 seal)
hypothesis: SOURCE: Jiang, Kelly & Xiu, '(Re-)Imag(in)ing Price Trends', Journal of Finance 78(6), 2023 (doi 10.1111/jofi.13268), replacing Lo, Mamaysky & Wang (2000) at the user's request. Instead of hand-coded patterns, a CNN learns which shapes in a 20-day chart image precede a rise. They report out-of-sample (2001-2019) weekly long-short decile Sharpe ratios of 6.75 equal-weight and 1.74 value-weight GROSS, with turnover near 700% a month. SPEC, copied from the paper: image I20 = 64x60 pixels, black background, white OHLC bars (3 pixels per day: open tick, high-low bar, close tick) built from adjusted returns, 20-day moving average line, volume bars in the bottom fifth, each image scaled to its own high/low range. Label = 1 if the close-to-close return over the next 5 days is positive (R5). CNN = 3 blocks of [5x3 conv (64, 128, 256 filters), batch norm, leaky ReLU, 2x1 max-pool], 50% dropout, fully connected, softmax; Xavier init; Adam lr 1e-5, batch 128; early stopping after 2 epochs without validation improvement; 5 independently trained models averaged. ONE images per stock per 5-session week. TRAINING: 2014-2019, random 70/30 train/validation split. TEST: every week 2020-01 to 2026-09, model frozen, never retrained. UNIVERSE: the daily database (1,499 stocks, today's members, survivor-biased; no micro-caps, which drive the paper's equal-weight result, so the value-weight 1.74 is the relevant comparison). PORTFOLIO: each week sort stocks into deciles on predicted up-probability; H-L = long decile 10, short decile 1, equal-weight. EXECUTION (stricter than the paper): enter at the NEXT OPEN after the image date, exit 5 sessions later at the open. COST: 5bp per unit of one-way turnover per leg; break-even cost also reported. PASS, both: (1) replication: gross H-L weekly return t >= 2.0 out of sample; (2) tradeable: net H-L t >= 2.0. Descriptive only: the paper's close-to-close timing, long-only decile 10 vs the equal-weight universe, turnover, by-year, and prediction accuracy.
name: chart-image CNN (Jiang, Kelly & Xiu 2023, J. Finance): learned chart patterns from 20-day price images

note: PRE-TEST DIAGNOSTIC (2026-10-14, while training, before any 2020-2026 data was scored). Probing finished model 1 on its own 2014-2019 validation charts: its score has no relationship to simple chart features (rank correlations -0.03 to +0.04 with position in range, 5- and 20-day return, distance from MA, volatility, volume trend). Its validation gains come from recognising WHICH WEEK a chart is from: 12% of score variance is the week, the week's average score correlates +0.58 with the week's average return, and deciles ranked across weeks span -67 to +117bp while deciles ranked WITHIN each week are flat (top minus bottom -4.3bp/week, t=-0.31, 60 weeks). Cause: the paper's random 70/30 split puts the same weeks in training and validation, so validation loss rewards memorising market-wide weekly moves and early stopping selects for it. The declared test still ranks within each week, so it remains valid, but a pass is less likely. A time-based validation split would fix this and would be a separate, newly declared trial.

hypothesis: Declared 2026-10-14 BEFORE trial 50's test results exist. Trial 50's pre-test diagnostic showed the paper's random 70/30 train/validation split lets validation loss reward recognising which WEEK a chart is from (market-wide moves), so early stopping can select a week-memoriser rather than a stock-picker. FIX: identical to trial 50 in every respect (same 867k images, same I20/R5 labels, same CNN, Xavier init, Adam 1e-5, batch 128, patience 2, max 30 epochs, 5 runs averaged, same test, same execution at the next open, same 5bp per unit traded, same deciles ranked within each week) EXCEPT the validation set: train on images dated before 2018-12-24 (so no 5-day label reaches 2019), validate on images dated 2019-01-01 to 2019-12-16. Validation weeks are then never seen in training, so a lower validation loss requires patterns that carry across time. PASS, both, as trial 50: (1) gross H-L t >= 2.0 on 2020-2026; (2) net H-L t >= 2.0. Descriptive: the same within-week probe on the 2019 validation set, and comparison with trial 50.

note: PRE-TEST DIAGNOSTIC 2 (2026-10-14 ~18:45, models 1-4 finished, model 5 training, no 2020-2026 data scored). FAIL on both. 5-model ensemble (best validation losses 0.689/0.684/0.686/0.682/0.699) scored once on 338 weeks 2020-01 to 2026-09, ~1,453 stocks a week, deciles ranked within week, entry next open, 5 sessions. Gross H-L -57.1bp/week, t=-1.18; net -75.0bp/week, t=-1.55, Sharpe -0.61. Accuracy 51.4% vs 52.7% for always 'up'. Turnover ~180% per leg per week. The model's MOST BEARISH decile earned the most (+91bp/week vs ~30-37bp for deciles 2-10): it ranked crashed stocks as likely to fall and they rebounded, dominated by 2020 (H-L -316.6bp/week); other years -35 to +8bp. note: PRE-RESULT CONTEXT (2026-10-14, trial 52 training; nothing scored). Read in full: Dixon & Zeng (Univ. of Melbourne), 'How does Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) predict stock returns?', working paper, July 2024, 51 pp. They re-implement Jiang-Kelly-Xiu on the same CRSP data (train 1993-2000, test 2001-2019); no post-2019 test; no transaction-cost analysis (they note weekly portfolio returns 'may not be practically achievable'). Their replication reproduces JKX closely for I5R5 (EW Sharpe 7.18 vs JKX 7.15; VW 1.57). For OUR target, I20/R20 monthly, their Table 8 gives equal-weight H-L Sharpe 1.84 but VALUE-WEIGHT 0.16, not significant ('At the monthly level, JKX value weighted portfolio is not significant at all'). They attribute most of the CNN signal to short-term reversal and the last day's close relative to its range (four simple variables explain 73% of weekly and 48% of monthly CNN returns), with the extreme deciles concentrated in small stocks. Implication: for large, liquid stocks at a monthly horizon, even 2001-2019 shows essentially no edge; trial 52's 2020-2026 test on 1,500 large and mid caps is expected to be weak. The verification gate (at least half of 2.16 on the authors' 2001-2019 equal-weight data) is unaffected: an independent team got 1.84.

VERIFIED, then FAIL as declared. STEP 1: on the authors' own 2001-2019 images the 5-model ensemble gives equal-weight monthly H-L +1.82%/month, t=10.67, Sharpe 2.45 (paper 2.16; Dixon-Zeng replication 1.84); value-weight Sharpe 0.53, t=2.29. Implementation confirmed. STEP 2, 80 months 2020-01 to 2026-08, ~1,454 stocks a month: as declared, gross H-L -2.18%/month t=-0.75, net -2.82% t=-0.97, Sharpe -0.38: FAIL. The concentration alarm fired (top-5 months carry 63%): the declared numbers are dominated by the known CHRD bankruptcy re-stitch (+30,991% 20-day 'return', Oct 2020, bottom decile; H-L -230% that month), a row already listed in reports/data_quality_flags.csv. Trimming each month at 0.5%/99.5% (trial 51's rule): gross +0.68% t=2.04 Sharpe 0.79; net +0.03% t=0.10 Sharpe 0.04. 500 largest by dollar volume (paper Table IV analogue), trimmed: gross +0.87% t=2.09 Sharpe 0.81; net +0.35% t=0.84 Sharpe 0.33. Reading: the chart-image signal still PREDICTS in 2020-2026 before costs (Sharpe about 0.7-0.8, t about 2, similar to the paper's large-stock evidence), but the paper's own cost rule removes essentially all of it for the full universe and leaves an insignificant Sharpe of about 0.3 in the 500 largest. Trimmed decile means are flat from decile 1 to 9 (+1.26 to +1.57%/month) with only decile 10 higher (+1.94%), so whatever signal exists sits in the long leg. A long-only top-decile strategy is a post-hoc idea from this data and would have to be a new, pre-declared trial on data not yet seen.

hypothesis: Replication gate, not a strategy search. Using the authors' published per-stock file (SampleForPaperRandomized.csv, Mendeley x63r376783 v2) and their own MLER forecasts, rebuild Table 3: each month sort stocks into deciles of MLER using NYSE-only breakpoints (NYSESample==1), value-weight by MktCapM (end of month t-1), 10-1 = decile 10 minus decile 1, return = RetRF in month t. hypothesis: The paper reports no transaction-cost or turnover analysis in 168 pages. hypothesis: Months after the paper's sample end (2022-12). hypothesis: Proper version of trials 53-56 now that WRDS/CRSP is available (crsp.msf_v2 through 2025-12-31). SAMPLE as the paper (SampleForFits.R): US common stocks (sharetype NS, securitytype EQTY, securitysubtype COM, US incorporated) on NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ, 12 prior monthly returns and t-1 market cap required. Returns from msf_v2 mthret, which already includes delisting returns (the paper used legacy msf plus its -30%/-100% rule; deviation recorded). Market cap = |price| x shares at t-1; NYSE = primaryexch N. Inputs CumRet1..12, target RetRFNorm, weight EWPM, CNN-LSTM, MSE, Adam, batch 32,768, early stopping on validation MAE patience 5, 30 runs averaged: identical to python/cbm_replication.py (PyTorch replica of their Keras code). GATE 1 (data and portfolio code, no ML): Mom and Rev value-weighted 10-1 with NYSE breakpoints, 1963-07 to 2022-12, must be within 0.25%/month of the paper's Table A12 (Mom +1.21, Rev -0.34). GATE 2 (model): expanding-window fits 1927-01..2004-12 and 1927-01..2014-12, scored on 2005-2014 and 2015-2022 respectively, value-weighted 10-1 with NYSE breakpoints; the monthly series must correlate >= 0.60 with the authors' real 10-1 returns (DailyMLERPortfolioExcessReturns.csv compounded) and each subperiod mean must be within 0.40%/month of theirs (-0.09 and +1.17). Neither gate passing means nothing below runs. COSTS, measured: one-way turnover from drift-adjusted value weights; 10bp per unit traded for stocks above the NYSE 20th size percentile, 20bp otherwise. TEST: fit 1927-01..2022-12, frozen, scored once on 2023-01 to 2025-12 (36 months, after the paper's sample). PASS, both: value-weighted 10-1 gross Newey-West t >= 2.0 AND net t >= 2.0 on 2023-2025. Also reported, not pass bars: net 2015-2022 with real turnover, top-500 version, minimum detectable effect, concentration alarm, and the pooled 2015-2025 net (overlapping the paper's own period, so not out of sample). CRSP data stays local and out of git (license).
